response: Yes, viral infections are believed to have a role in benign paroxysmal positional vertigo (BPPV). Research has found that BPPV is associated with positive viral serology, particularly during certain months of the year, mainly in spring and autumn. It is thought that viral infection might promote BPPV attacks due to the development of vestibulopathy or induce secondary BPPV via viral infection-related neurolabyrinthitis.
